explainer_content.short_definition: The theatrical 1970s rock road where persona, glitter, gender play, costume, and artifice become as audible as riffs and hooks.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Glam rock turns performance into argument. Bowie, T. Rex, Roxy Music, Lou Reed, Queen, and related artists use makeup, alter egos, camp, alienation, and flash to make rock feel self-conscious, stylish, and unstable.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It opened a path for art pop, punk style, new wave, arena theatricality, queer pop signaling, and the idea that identity can be staged rather than confessed plainly.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: The record often winks at you. It wants you to hear the song and see the character at the same time.
what_to_listen_for: Riffs that are simple but stylized
Lyrics about stars, outsiders, desire, or performance
Stacked vocals or dramatic arrangement flourishes
Image and sound reinforcing each other
